note: Baseline for `bun run test`. `units` = tests bun reported SKIPPED per run unit; `counts` = tests Bun reported completed per run unit; `failing` = failures PINNED as known, by name. All three are ratchets: any change fails the run and prints what moved. Pin only failures that are understood and filed — never to make a red go away. Counts seeded from the 2026-09-04 fast tier after the worker framing and dependency-ledger fixes.

The refactor sweep deleted the unused provider surface and its tests (`test/exports.test.ts`, `test/provider/cloudflare.test.ts`, `test/provider/openrouter.test.ts` and others); one of those files carried a skipped test, so the skip left with the file it lived in. reasons.novaclaw:server: NO pins — this unit is expected FULLY GREEN, and any failure is drift. The empty `failing` entry is documentary: it is inert to the matcher (a pin needs a non-empty set) and exists only so this reason has a unit to hang on. ⚠️ A flake belongs in quarantine, never here — this unit has produced different new failures on consecutive runs under memory pressure, and an environmental failure pinned as expected is an expectation that can never come true.

hostCommitWarnPctNote: Per-unit host-commit WARNING lines; anything absent uses the default 75% (heavy-guard's admission line, and the product's own Pressure warning). `core` is here because a flat 75 fired on 15 of its 31 recorded runs -- its MEDIAN host commit is 74% and its max is 80% -- while NO other unit has ever reached 75 at all. A warning that fires on half of a unit's healthy runs is one its reader learns to skip. 85 is derived from core's observed max (80) plus margin, measured 2026-08-13 over 348 unit-rows across 17 full gates. ⚠️ It therefore inherits that measurement's expiry date: if core's normal band moves, re-derive this rather than nudging it. The 90% FLOOR is a separate, product-wide line and is NOT per-unit.
workingSetsNote: Resident WorkingSet64 peak per run unit -- the RESIDENT half of the two-wall ladder in script/lib/memory-plan.ts. Missing units use the explicit UNPROFILED_RESIDENT_MB default; never infer resident demand from commit charge. RE-BASELINED WHOLE on 2026-09-02 from tmp/peak-series.jsonl, because the concurrent runner turned this map from an advisory into a BUDGET: with only `core` measured, every other unit reserved the 1200 MB GUESS -- 3-10x the measured peak for most of them -- and that alone capped the pool at one unit on a loaded box. Filter = peaksNote's three exclusions PLUS the host-pressure term the 2026-09-01 peaksLadderNote ruling asked for: ok, shards 1, 3+ own ticks, regressed != true, carrying foreignMb (post-attribution rows only), carrying hostCommitPct, and hostCommitPct BELOW that unit's hostCommitWarnPct line (85 for core, 75 otherwise). Each entry is then the LARGEST surviving reading; WHOLE_HEADROOM_FACTOR covers overshoot beyond it. THREE units are left ABSENT on fewer than 10 surviving rows and keep the declared guess: effect-drizzle-sqlite (n=2), `novaclaw test/*` (n=9, max 3791) and `novaclaw test/worker-watch-wiring.test.ts` (n=2). WARNING core moved 4616 -> 4861 under this filter and that is not a regression: 4616 was a single 2026-08-09 measurement, and 4861 is the max of 19 quiet runs. The pressure term is what excludes the 7300-8000 MB readings of 2026-08-26..29 -- every one of which is also regressed:true, i.e. the episode the ratchet caught, which peaksNote already says is not a baseline. Evidence: notes/reports/gate-concurrency-2026-09-02.md.
peaksNote: Measured peak MB per run unit - the input to the memory ladder in script/lib/memory-plan.ts. RE-BASELINED WHOLE on 2026-08-13 from the attributed rows of tmp/peak-series.jsonl, superseding the 2026-08-07 baseline. Each entry is the LARGEST HEALTHY WHOLE-RUN reading for that unit; WHOLE_HEADROOM_FACTOR then covers overshoot beyond that maximum. THREE exclusions, each of which a naive max gets wrong: (1) SHARDED rows, because a shard's window carries the previous shard's unreclaimed memory - that is why `core` read 17,958 while no whole run ever exceeded 10,822, and feeding it back is what kept core permanently sharded; (2) rows with fewer than 3 own-ticks, which are lower bounds; (3) rows flagged `regressed: true`, because a regression the ratchet caught is not a baseline - a plain max would have enshrined novaclaw:server at 9,303 and app:unit at 1,918, the exact rows that went red. `schema` is kept at its 2026-08-07 value on purpose: it is a FLOOR from an under-sampled bound, and the healthy series has only 2 rows. Piecemeal editing is how the dead 1007 MB core entry survived four gates, so re-baseline the set or none of it.
peaksScaleNote: 🔴 ROWS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS 2026-08-07 app 2d6ad8db7. Before it the sampler summed every `bun` on the box by name and every reading also carried the `bun run test` parent shim; after it a sample is attributed by process BIRTH TIME and carries `foreignMb`. No arithmetic converts an old row into a new one — `schema` read 43 (the shim alone, its own process caught by no tick) and reads 552-1236 now. Only rows carrying `foreignMb` were used here. See todo/test-speed.md.
peaksUnsampledNote: TWO units have no entry ON PURPOSE and must not be given one from the series: `script` and `effect-drizzle-sqlite`. Absent, they plan with UNPROFILED_PEAK_MB (1200), a declared guess. CORRECTED 2026-08-13: the original reason was 'no attributed run reached 3 own-ticks', and for `script` that is no longer true -- 28 runs now have 3+ ticks, max 345 MB, so the tool started printing 'copy it into peaks'. Do NOT. Across the whole series `script` has been observed at 625 MB, so its well-sampled runs are missing the peak by nearly 2x; 3 samples is enough to stop LOOKING thin, not enough to have SEEN the peak. Writing 345 in would under-reserve against a real observation, which is the same bug in a new disguise. `effect-drizzle-sqlite` still has only 2 well-sampled runs (max 634) against a 688 MB observation. Both are now listed in `peaksDeliberatelyAbsent`, which `script/test.ts` reads, so the printed advice and this note can no longer disagree. `schema` is the exception and is listed in `peaks`: it is equally under-sampled, but its largest bound (1236) EXCEEDS the 1200 guess, so the guess is falsified and the bound is the safer of the two. Its entry is a floor, not a peak.
peaksLadderNote: Commit and resident demand are planned against independent walls as of 2026-08-09; never collapse them through min(free RAM, commit headroom). CORRECTED 2026-09-01: this note used to say `core` carries a 17958 MB commit profile. It does not, and has not since the 2026-08-13 whole re-baseline three lines up -- 17958 was a SHARDED row, which is exactly what peaksNote excludes. The live pair is peaks.core 10822 commit / workingSets.core 4616 resident. Re-measured 2026-09-01 over healthy whole runs in tmp/peak-series.jsonl (shards 1, not regressed, 3+ own ticks, carrying foreignMb): 44 core runs span 7921-16310 MB commit and 2422-7971 MB resident. SIX of the 44 exceed the committed 10822, and all six are 2026-08-25 runs taken at 74-85% host commit -- so peaks.core may now be an under-reservation on a loaded box and wants a re-baseline, not an edit here. Sharding core still mitigates little because the bulk of its commit belongs to sixteen bun workers spawned by one flock test file. RULING 2026-09-01, on the six: DO NOT raise peaks.core to fit them. The healthiness filter used for that re-measurement (shards 1, not regressed, 3+ own ticks, carrying foreignMb) has NO host-pressure term, so it cannot see the one thing those six share -- they were taken at 74-85% host commit, i.e. inside the band this same file already distrusts via hostCommitWarnPct.core = 85. They are not healthy runs that exceed the ceiling; they are contended runs the filter is blind to. Raising 10822 toward 16310 would bake machine contention into a UNIT's profile and leave the ratchet unable to see a real ~50% regression -- a bound that measures the probe rather than the subject, which is the failure this whole ladder exists to avoid. The fix is to give the healthiness filter a host-pressure term (reuse hostCommitWarnPct) and re-measure over quiet runs only; if the quiet population still exceeds 10822, THAT is a re-baseline and it is earned. Whoever does it: report how many runs survived the pressure filter, because a ceiling re-derived from a handful of samples is the same mistake one level down.
